extracted.intended_audience: F-1 students, designated school officials (DSOs), employers, and immigration practitioners
extracted.subtask_short: F-1 OPT/CPT and STEM OPT rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing F-1 curricular practical training (CPT), optional practical training (OPT), the 24-month STEM OPT extension, related employer/DSO obligations, reporting, filing deadlines, unemployment limits, reinstatement, and special rules for dependents and border commuter students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular practical training (CPT) authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student may be authorized by the DSO to participate in a curricular practical training program that is an integral part of an established curriculum (alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education, required internship or practicum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students who have received one year or more of full-time CPT are ineligible for post-completion academic training, with exceptions for graduate studies that require immediate participation in CPT. A request for authorization must be made to the DSO; the student may begin CPT only after receiving Form I-20 (or successor) with DSO endorsement. The DSO must update SEVIS to indicate CPT authorization, whether full- or part-time, employer and location, start and end dates, and must sign/date/return the Form I-20 prior to employment commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Practical Training (OPT) general eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A student may apply to USCIS for authorization for temporary employment for OPT directly related to the student's major area of study and may not begin OPT until the date on the Employment Authorization Document (EAD, Form I-766).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPT may be granted: (1) during annual vacation and other times when school is not in session if enrolled and intending to register for next term; (2) while school is in session provided practical training does not exceed 20 hours/week during session; (3) after completion of the course of study (or after all course requirements excluding thesis). All practical training must be completed within 14 months following completion of study, except that a 24-month STEM extension need not be completed within that 14-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of optional practical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization to engage in OPT employment is automatically terminated when the student transfers to another school or begins study at another educational level.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-month STEM OPT extension overview and lifetime cap
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified student in a STEM field may apply for a 24-month extension of post-completion OPT while in a valid period of post-completion OPT; extensions are limited to two lifetime STEM OPT extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 17-month extension previously granted is counted as one STEM extension; a subsequent 24-month extension must be based on a degree at a higher degree level than the degree that formed the basis for the first OPT extension. In no event more than two lifetime STEM OPT extensions are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation requirement for STEM OPT extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree that is the basis for the 24-month OPT extension must be from a U.S. educational institution accredited by an accrediting agency recognized by the Department of Education at the time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS-approved degree / STEM Designated Degree Program List
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifying degree must be a bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in a field determined to qualify as science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) per the Department of Education's Classification of Instructional Programs taxonomy or related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary (or designee) will maintain the STEM Designated Degree Program List published on the SEVP website; all program categories on the list must be consistent with the definition in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree inclusion at time of DSO recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time the DSO recommends a 24-month OPT extension in SEVIS, the degree that is the basis for the application must be contained within a category on the STEM Designated Degree Program List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility when based on previously obtained STEM degree
rubrics_metrics.description: A degree used as the basis for a 24-month OPT extension may be a previously obtained degree (not necessarily the degree that provided the basis for the initial post-completion OPT), but that previously obtained degree must have been conferred from a U.S. accredited and SEVP-certified institution and be on the current STEM list at the time of the DSO recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The previously obtained degree must have been conferred within the 10 years preceding the date the DSO recommends the student for the 24-month extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM practical training opportunity must be directly related to qualifying degree
rubrics_metrics.description: The STEM practical training opportunity that is the basis for the 24-month OPT extension must be directly related to the degree that qualifies the student for such extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The degree used to qualify may be the previously obtained degree described in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer E-Verify and EIN requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The student's employer must be enrolled in E-Verify (evidenced by valid E-Verify Company ID or Client Company ID) and remain a participant in good standing, and must have an employer identification number (EIN) used for tax purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer reporting obligation for STEM OPT (termination/departure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer must agree, by signing Form I-983 (or successor), to report the termination or departure of an OPT student to the student's DSO within five business days if the termination/departure occurs prior to the end of the authorized period of OPT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employer considers a student to have departed when the employer knows the student has left the opportunity, or if the student has not reported for practical training for five consecutive business days without employer consent, whichever occurs earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-983 (Training Plan) completion and submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must fully complete an individualized Form I-983 (or successor) and obtain requisite employer signatures before the DSO may recommend a 24-month OPT extension in SEVIS; the student must submit the signed form to the DSO at the institution of most recent enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A student while in F-1 status may also be required to submit Form I-983 to ICE and/or USCIS upon request or per form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training plan content requirements (Form I-983)
rubrics_metrics.description: The training plan must identify goals for the STEM practical training opportunity, including specific knowledge, skills, or techniques to be imparted, explain how goals will be achieved through the work-based learning, describe a performance evaluation process, and describe methods of oversight and supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers may rely on existing training programs or policies to satisfy performance evaluation and oversight/supervision requirements, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training plan must explain relation to qualifying STEM degree
rubrics_metrics.description: The Form I-983 (or successor) must explain how the training is directly related to the student's qualifying STEM degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: New employer during STEM extension requires new Form I-983 and DSO recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student begins a new practical training opportunity with a new employer during the 24-month extension, the student must submit a new Form I-983 (or successor) to the DSO within 10 days of beginning the new opportunity and obtain a new DSO recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties, hours, and compensation must be commensurate with similarly situated U.S. workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms and conditions of a STEM practical training opportunity (duties, hours, compensation) must be commensurate with terms applicable to the employer's similarly situated U.S. workers in the area of employment; students may not engage in training for less than 20 hours/week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employer does not employ/recently employ more than two similarly situated U.S. workers, employer still must attest commensurateness. 'Similarly situated U.S. workers' includes workers with similar duties, supervision, educational background, expertise, experience, responsibility and skill sets. 'Commensurate' means duties/hours/compensation are consistent with the range employer has offered or would offer to similarly situated U.S. employees. Student must disclose compensation on Form I-983.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation requirements and training plan modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must submit required evaluations of progress toward training goals: an initial evaluation within 12 months of the approved start date and a concluding evaluation; evaluations must be signed by the student and appropriate employer official and submitted to the DSO as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All evaluations must be completed prior to the conclusion of the STEM practical training opportunity; the student is responsible for ensuring the DSO receives 12-month and final evaluations no later than 10 days following the conclusion of the reporting period or training. Material changes or deviations to the training plan (examples: change of EIN from corporate restructuring, reduction in compensation not tied to hours reduction, significant decrease in hours, hours below 20/week) require a modified Form I-983 signed by student and employer and submitted to the DSO at the earliest opportunity. Material changes also include any change that renders an employer attestation or Form I-983 information inaccurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional recordkeeping and access for I-983 and evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: The educational institution whose DSO is responsible for the student's latest OPT extension must ensure SEVP has access to each individualized Form I-983 (or successor) and associated student evaluations, including through SEVIS if technologically available, beginning within 30 days after submission to the DSO and continuing for three years following completion of each STEM opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer attestations for STEM OPT (resources, non-replacement, training benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: For STEM practical training the employer must attest (including by signing Form I-983) that: (i) the employer has sufficient resources and personnel to provide appropriate training at the specified location(s); (ii) the student will not replace a U.S. worker (full/part-time, temporary or permanent); and (iii) the opportunity assists the student in reaching training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS site visit authority and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS may conduct a site visit of any employer to ensure the employer possesses and maintains the ability and resources to provide structured and guided work-based learning consistent with Form I-983.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will provide 48 hours' notice to the employer prior to site visits, except notice may not be provided if the visit is triggered by a complaint or other evidence of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of status while on post-completion OPT
rubrics_metrics.description: For a student with approved post-completion OPT, duration of status begins on the date the student's OPT application was properly filed and pending approval (including the authorized OPT period) and ends 60 days after the OPT employment authorization expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemployment day limits during OPT and STEM extension
rubrics_metrics.description: During post-completion OPT, students may not accrue more than 90 days of aggregate unemployment; students granted a 24-month OPT extension may not accrue more than 150 days of aggregate unemployment during the total OPT period (including initial and extension periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPT application filing and deadlines (student responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must initiate OPT by requesting a recommendation from the DSO, obtain a signed Form I-20 showing the recommendation, and properly file Form I-765 (Application for Employment Authorization) with USCIS with the required fee and supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-completion OPT: file up to 90 days before being enrolled for one full academic year (employment will not start before completion of that year). Post-completion OPT (excluding STEM extension): file up to 90 days before program end date and no later than 60 days after program end date, and file Form I-765 within 30 days of the DSO entering the recommendation into SEVIS. 24-month extension: file Form I-765 up to 90 days prior to current OPT expiration and within 60 days of the DSO entering the recommendation into SEVIS. If the current EAD expires before decision and the student timely/properly filed, the EAD is automatically extended per 8 CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date restrictions for OPT employment
rubrics_metrics.description: A student may not begin OPT employment prior to the approved start date on the EAD (Form I-766) and may not request a start date more than 60 days after the program end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization begins on the requested date or the date the EAD is adjudicated, whichever is later. Exception provisions described elsewhere apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSO responsibilities for OPT recommendations and SEVIS updates
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must have a DSO recommendation to apply for OPT. The DSO assumes responsibility for maintaining the student's SEVIS record for the period of authorized OPT and must ensure student eligibility prior to recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to recommending a 24-month STEM extension the DSO must certify the degree is shown in SEVIS or official transcripts and is on the STEM list, and may only recommend if Form I-983 has been properly completed and executed. A DSO may not recommend if the employer fails to meet regulatory requirements. The DSO must update SEVIS with the recommendation before the student applies, indicate whether OPT is full- or part-time (or meets the minimum hours for STEM extension), and note start/end dates. The DSO must provide the student with a signed/dated Form I-20 indicating OPT recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS adjudication, notice, and no appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will adjudicate Form I-765 based on the DSO's recommendation and other eligibility considerations, will notify the applicant in writing of the decision and reasons for denial, and the applicant may not appeal the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, employment authorization period begins on the requested date or approval date per rules; for STEM extension begins day after expiration of initial post-completion OPT and ends 24 months thereafter regardless of approval date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations while on OPT
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student granted OPT employment authorization is required to report any change of name or address, or interruption of such employment to the DSO for the duration of the OPT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommending DSO is responsible for updating the student's SEVIS record to reflect reported changes while training is authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional reporting and validation requirements for 24-month STEM OPT
rubrics_metrics.description: Students with an approved 24-month STEM OPT extension must report within 10 days any change of legal name, residential/mailing address, employer name/address, and/or loss of employment; and must complete a validation report confirming required information every six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The validation reporting requirement starts on the 24-month extension begin date and ends when F-1 status expires or the extension concludes, whichever first. Validation reports are due to the DSO within 10 business days of each reporting date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and reentry during OPT (temporary absence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A student returning from a temporary trip abroad with an unexpired off-campus employment authorization on Form I-20 may resume employment only if readmitted to attend the same school that granted the authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An F-1 student with an unexpired EAD for post-completion practical training who is otherwise admissible may return to the U.S. to resume employment after temporary absence if the EAD is used in combination with a Form I-20 endorsed for reentry by the DSO within the last six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of strike or other labor dispute on employment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employment authorization is automatically suspended upon certification by the Secretary of Labor (or designee) that a strike or other labor dispute involving a work stoppage is in progress in the occupation at the place of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer is prohibited from transferring F-1 students working at other facilities to the facility where the work stoppage is occurring. 'Place of employment' means the facility or facilities where the labor dispute exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-2 spouse and children issuance and employment prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: F-2 spouse and minor children of an F-1 student will each be issued an individual Form I-20; F-2 spouse and children may not accept employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-2 post-secondary/vocational study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-2 spouse or child may enroll in less-than-full course of study in specified programs at SEVP-certified schools but is not eligible for employment; full course of study at post-secondary level requires change of status to F-1, M-1 or J-1 before beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study that is avocational or recreational may be undertaken, up to full-time. Enrollment to complete a course during a term does not by itself make attendance a full course of study for undergraduate/community college students.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-2 elementary or secondary study
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-2 child may engage in full-time study in any elementary or secondary school (kindergarten through twelfth grade).

rubrics_metrics.name: F-2 violation by enrolling in unauthorized study
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-2 spouse and child violates nonimmigrant status by enrolling in any study except as provided in the regulations for post-secondary/vocational and elementary/secondary study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement to student status eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may consider reinstating a student who files Form I-539 with a properly completed Form I-20 showing DSO recommendation if the student meets regulatory criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include: not out of status for more than 5 months at filing (unless exceptional circumstances and filed as promptly as possible); no record of repeated or willful violations; currently pursuing or intending to pursue full course of study at the school that issued the Form I-20; has not engaged in unauthorized employment; not deportable on certain grounds; and must establish either that the violation resulted from circumstances beyond the student's control (examples: serious injury/illness, institution closure, natural disaster, DSO inadvertence) or that the violation relates to a reduction in course load that a DSO could have authorized and failure to reinstate would cause extreme hardship. The adjudicating officer will update SEVIS; reinstatement denials are not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to report legal name and address changes and SEVIS update timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must inform DHS and the DSO of any legal changes to name or any change of address within 10 days; the DSO must enter the information in SEVIS within 21 days of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address provided must be the actual physical location of residence (not a mailing address) except where student cannot receive mail; if a mailing address is provided, school must maintain record of and provide upon request the actual physical location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for border commuter students
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'border commuter student' (Canadian or Mexican national admitted as F-1 to enroll in a full course of study on a part-time basis in a school within 75 miles of a U.S. land border) must maintain actual residence in home country and seek admission at a land border POE; special rules apply to course load, period of admission, and employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSO may authorize reduced course load consistent with commuter's certified course of study; DSO must specify a completion date on Form I-20 that reflects actual semester/term dates; a new Form I-20 is required for each new semester/term; duration of status and extension provisions do not apply to border commuter students. Employment is generally not authorized except for CPT or post-completion OPT as specified in regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remittance of SEVIS fee for F-1/F-3 applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who applies for F-1 or F-3 nonimmigrant status to enroll at an SEVP-certified institution is required to pay the SEVIS fee to DHS per 8 CFR 214.13, except as provided in that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives to international organizations classification and extension statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination by a consular officer prior to admission and recognition by the Secretary of State after admission is evidence of proper classification under section 101(a)(15)(G); for certain G categories admission is for specified initial periods with possible extensions of temporary stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application for extension of temporary stay must be accompanied by a statement signed by the employing official stating intent to continue employment and describing type of work the applicant will perform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of G-1, G-3, or G-4 dependent for employment purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For employment purposes, a 'dependent' of a G-1, G-3, or G-4 principal alien means immediate family members habitually residing in same household: spouse; unmarried children under 21; unmarried sons or daughters under 23 in full-time attendance at post-secondary institutions; unmarried sons/daughters under 25 in full-time attendance if covered by certain bilateral agreements; unmarried disabled sons/daughters; or other immediate family members designated by Department of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some provisions apply only to G-1 and G-3 dependents under certain bilateral agreements and not to G-4 dependents; Department of State/Service may require certifications to document disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of bilateral agreement or de facto arrangements for G-1 and G-3 dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of a formal bilateral agreement for G-1 and G-3 dependents is based on the foreign state which employs the principal alien, not on the nationality of the principal alien or dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions referenced apply only where the foreign state has such a formal bilateral agreement; Office of Protocol maintains a listing of foreign states with such agreements.
